diagnosis.root_cause: EPON0/7 is not admitting or maintaining ONU registration: every sampled ONU on the port is offline, has no optical reading, and reports MPCP DEREG/Unauth. The shared-port pattern and sharp traffic reduction indicate a PON-port-side failure rather than an individual ONU, fibre, laser, RADIUS, VLAN, router, or OLT chassis problem.
evidence: The subscriber and all sampled peers on EPON0/7 are offline, while their OLT records still respond; this is a shared access-side failure pattern.
Live ONU probes show online=false, null RX/TX readings, auth_flag=Unauth, and MPCP DEREG for all eight sampled ONUs.

The subscriber's historical RX power around -21.4 dBm, TX power around +2.35 dBm, constant 166 m distance, stable bias current around 11.2 mA, and stable supply voltage were all healthy before the current outage.
There is no optical degradation trend, distance change, laser-ageing signature, or evidence of an individual fibre or ONU fault.
Traffic on EPON0/7 is currently 6 Mbps versus a 219 Mbps average and 660 Mbps peak, consistent with loss of most or all customers on the port.

RADIUS records match CRM, the customer VLAN is present and correct, session activity is not flapping, and the router heartbeat is healthy; these exclude authentication, provisioning, VLAN, and router causes.
The OLT itself responds to ping and SNMP and has normal CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime, so an OLT chassis failure is not supported.
The stored zero optical values and recent telemetry gaps are no-reading conditions caused by the ONU offline state, not strong optical readings or evidence of fibre degradation.
The OLT health result is inconsistent with the live EPON0/7 evidence and should be treated as an unreliable port-health result until the port is directly checked.

remediation.action: Open a PON-port outage ticket for EPON0/7 and dispatch access/OLT operations to inspect the port optics, PON transceiver, connectorization, splitter feed, and port configuration. Check OLT alarms and counters, reset or fail over the PON interface if operationally safe, and move affected ONUs to a spare PON port if the port hardware is defective. Do not replace the subscriber ONU or change RADIUS/VLAN settings before the shared-port fault is resolved.

ground_truth.root_cause: The health check marks an OLT critical only when every sampled PON fails. Seven of eight failed here, so it wrote 'healthy' with a null error description while healthy_pons stood at 1 of 8 in the same record. A genuine multi-port outage is running underneath a healthy verdict.
expected_reasoning: The health record reports overall_status healthy with a null error description
The same record holds healthy_pons 1 against total_pons_tested 8, and seven entries in failed_pons_list
The summary label contradicts the detail fields inside one record
The check sets critical only when every sampled PON fails, so seven of eight yields healthy by design
Probing confirms every ONU on EPON0/7 returns responds true with online 0, a definite negative
oid_subtree_responds is true, so this is not the firmware mismatch mechanism
43 of 272 customers on the OLT are offline, far above the 4.85% background rate
Sessions ended together and PON traffic has collapsed from 219 to 6 Mbps
This is a genuine multi-port outage that the health check's status rule conceals

expected_escalation.review_reason: The health check reported healthy during a seven-port outage; the status rule needs correcting

distractors: The health record says healthy, inviting a no_fault conclusion
A scheduled scan with no complaint gives no reason to look harder
The fault type is a health check defect but the service impact is real
